A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAEmoLLM and contain readable main text, algorithms, tables, figures and appendices. Their shared methods and experiments can be matched reliably despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on AMTCele, PHEME and COCO, including per-domain results, retrieval sensitivity studies and affective analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, embedding comparisons, statistical analyses and runtime measurements in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 removes v1's cosine-score threshold of 0.2, leaving unconditional scoring before top-K selection. This changes the reported retrieval procedure, while the affective encoder, three-module architecture and inference templates remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use AMTCele's seven domains, PHEME's nine events and the same held-out COCO topics: Fake Virus, Harmful Radiation and Depopulation. Added diagnostic analyses reuse these datasets without expanding benchmark task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds evaluated domain-generalization comparators MDFEND, EDDFN, MOSE, CANMD and MetaAdapt. Table 4 additionally compares retrieval using RoBERTa semantic embeddings and SentiBERT embeddings. These substantially extend v1's comparisons with fine-tuned BERT/RoBERTa and zero-shot/random few-shot methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama3.2 1B/3B configurations and protocols for embedding-substitution controls, source-identification probing and stage-level timing. Benchmark partitions, weighted classification metrics and retrieval-count ranges remain unchanged. Newly disclosed generation parameters do not establish that earlier settings differed.

E4.justification: v2 adds embedding-type ablations, a possible data-leakage diagnostic, timing against BERT and categorical-affect association tests. Conversely, v1's PCA dimensionality sensitivity and time-F1 trade-off studies disappear. Retrieval-count sensitivity and special-case analyses are retained with revised results and placement, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix G.2 and Table 12 add chi-squared independence tests and p-values for categorical affect versus misinformation labels across all three datasets. Existing affective means, variances and t-tests are retained. Benchmark seed counts, repeated-run variability and confidence intervals remain unreported.

E6.justification: Main, per-domain, retrieval-count and special-case scores are extensively revised, alongside new comparator and diagnostic results. For example, Mistral-7b Vreg-addexpl F1 changes from 0.7767/0.6935/0.7725 in v1 Table 4 to 0.7717/0.6920/0.7931 in v2 Table 3. These are revised reports, not established same-setting gains: v1 selects results across embedding dimensions, while v2 omits an equivalent selection description.

T1.justification: No theoretical propositions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations are added or revised. The affect definitions are retained and relocated; the added significance tests constitute empirical statistical analysis.

C1.justification: The headline gains shift from comparisons with zero-shot methods (20.69%, 23.94%, 39.11%) to other few-shot methods (15.64%, 31.18%, 15.73%), with the latter numbers calculated against random few-shot in Section 3.3.1. The central novelty claim of affect-based, fine-tuning-free cross-domain retrieval and inference remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving dataset size and COVID-specific emotional consistency, interprets its timing comparison as greater efficiency, and explicitly notes that rumours include true, false and unverified cases. Existing imbalance and short-text limitations remain, although the named PHEME failure examples narrow to Prince Toronto.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies an A100 80GB GPU, 256 maximum new tokens, do_sample=False, remaining generation defaults and extraction details for the new embedding baselines. It reports stage-level timings and changes the repository statement from planned release to availability. Conversely, v1's PCA construction and best-dimension selection details are omitted.

R1.justification: The expanded related work adds substantial discussion of domain-generalization methods, retrieval-augmented misinformation detection and demonstration selection, including newly cited works by Nan, Silva, Yue, Wang, Xuan and others. This broadens the research positioning beyond v1's shorter treatment. The Marimont and Shapiro dimensionality citation is removed.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves to Appendix A, dataset preprocessing enters Methodology, special cases move to Appendix D, and retrieval-count analysis enters a module-ablation subsection. The abstract and experimental discussion are rewritten, affective explanations are redistributed, and the standalone ethics statement disappears.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for embedding controls, source identification, runtime and chi-squared tests; splits and relocates existing affect-statistics tables; and expands the main comparison table. Figure 2's bars and axes change, Figure 7's class labels are corrected, and v1 Figures 11 and 12 are removed. Most remaining affect plots are reused.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct retrieval alternatives and relevant domain-generalization comparators, leaving important gaps in evaluating its central contribution. v2 Tables 3 and 4 substantially strengthen that evaluation, supported by clearer implementation disclosures. Removing the PCA trade-off study reduces supporting analysis, and the source-identification example does not establish training-data leakage, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the stronger comparative validation.
